record.original_question: Is the additivity number add(U_fin(Γ, O)) equal to b?

evidence.quote: Notes added in proof. Zdomskyy, in a series of recent works, settled (or partially settled) some of the problems mentioned in the paper, the answers being: “Yes” for Problem 5.1, “No” for Problem 8.6, and “Consistently yes” for Problem 11.2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a topological space (specifically, a set of reals or, more generally, a Lindelöf topological space). Recall the following selection principle. An open cover U of X is a γ-cover if it is infinite and every point of X belongs to all but finitely many members of U. Let Γ denote the family of all open γ-covers of X, and let O denote the family of all open covers of X.

The selection principle U_fin(Γ, O) asserts: for every sequence (U_n : n ∈ ω) of open γ-covers of X, there exist finite subfamilies F_n ⊆ U_n such that the family {⋃ F_n : n ∈ ω} is an open cover of X.

For a class P of topological spaces (here, P = U_fin(Γ, O), identified with the class of spaces satisfying this selection principle), the additivity number add(P) is defined as the least cardinality of a family F ⊆ P of subspaces of the real line such that ⋃ F ∉ P.

Let b denote the bounding number, i.e., the least cardinality of an unbounded family in (ω^ω, ≤*), where f ≤* g means f(n) ≤ g(n) for all but finitely many n.

Question: Is add(U_fin(Γ, O)) = b?
artifact.status_search_result: Work by L. Zdomskyy resolved this question negatively: it is consistent that add(U_fin(Γ, O)) < b, so the equality does not hold in ZFC. This is documented in Zdomskyy's papers on selection principles and in the "Notes added in proof" of the problem list itself.
